articles.title: “Reel-Obsessed Wife, Lover Kill Husband; Body Found in Salt-Filled Drum in Alwar”
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Alwar, Rajasthan – A chilling murder has come to light in Alwar district where 30-year-old Hansram alias Suraj, a labourer from Shahjahanpur (UP), was brutally killed by his wife Lakshmi Devi alias Sunita and her lover Jitendra.

body.html:
Alwar, Rajasthan – A chilling murder has come to light in Alwar district where 30-year-old Hansram alias Suraj, a labourer from Shahjahanpur (UP), was brutally killed by his wife Lakshmi Devi alias Sunita and her lover Jitendra.

Police said the victim’s decapitated body was stuffed inside a blue plastic drum and hidden on the terrace of their rented house. To avoid detection, the accused allegedly filled the drum with salt to hasten decomposition.

Hansram, recently unemployed, wanted to return to his native village. However, his wife, reportedly active on social media reels and in an affair with Jitendra, conspired to eliminate him.

After the crime, Sunita fled with her three children and the landlord’s son but was later arrested along with Jitendra. Police confirmed the killing was pre-planned and uncovered through tracking their movements.

The brutal method and the “social media angle” have sparked nationwide shock, drawing comparisons with earlier “drum murder” cases.

body.html:
Jaipur – On August 15, retired Army Captain Narsa Ram Jajda (64) was killed in a hit-and-run while cycling on Gandhi Path. CCTV footage showed an SUV, allegedly driven by Surbhi Maheswari, ramming into him and dragging his body nearly 10 feet before fleeing.

Residents staged protests demanding stricter road safety measures, including speed breakers and regular patrolling in areas used by senior citizens for morning walks and cycling.

The case has ignited debate on reckless driving, VIP treatment, and the urgent need for stronger road safety enforcement in Jaipur.

articles.title: ‘Is This a Joke?’: Gauhati HC Slams 3,000-Bigha Land Allotment to Cement Firm in Dima Hasao
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Guwahati – The Gauhati High Court has come down heavily on the Assam government and Mahabal Cements over the allotment of nearly 3,000 bighas of land in Dima Hasao’s Umrangso region, an ecologically rich area known for hot springs, migratory birds, and wildlife.

body.html:
Guwahati – The Gauhati High Court has come down heavily on the Assam government and Mahabal Cements over the allotment of nearly 3,000 bighas of land in Dima Hasao’s Umrangso region, an ecologically rich area known for hot springs, migratory birds, and wildlife.

During the hearing of Sonesh Hojai and 21 Ors vs State of Assam and 6 Ors, Justice Sanjay Kumar Medhi expressed disbelief when informed that such a vast tract had been allotted. A viral courtroom video shows him asking:
“3,000 bighas? The entire district? Is this some kind of joke?”

The company’s counsel described the land as “barren” and argued it was required for a cement factory. Justice Medhi, however, retorted: “We know how barren it is. Public interest must come first.”

The judge directed the North Cachar Hills Autonomous Council (NCHAC) to submit documents on the land allotment policy. The case, involving petitions from locals opposing eviction and a counter-plea by Mahabal Cements, will be heard again on September 1.

The matter has ignited debate over corporate land acquisition, environmental safeguards, and tribal rights under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution.

articles.title: Meerut Shock: Army Jawan Brutally Beaten ‘Taliban-Style’ at Toll Plaza
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Meerut, UP – In a shocking case of hooliganism, Indian Army soldier Kapil, posted in Kashmir, was brutally assaulted at Bhuni Toll Plaza in Sarurpur on Sunday night (Aug 17). Kapil, returning to duty after leave, showed his Army ID and sought quick passage during a traffic jam.

body.html:
Meerut, UP – In a shocking case of hooliganism, Indian Army soldier Kapil, posted in Kashmir, was brutally assaulted at Bhuni Toll Plaza in Sarurpur on Sunday night (Aug 17).

Kapil, returning to duty after leave, showed his Army ID and sought quick passage during a traffic jam. This sparked an argument with toll staff, who, along with local miscreants, allegedly tied him to a pole and thrashed him with sticks and kicks, in Taliban-style brutality.

His cousin Shivam, travelling with him, was also beaten. Both sustained serious injuries. Disturbing CCTV and viral videos show the assault, sparking outrage nationwide.

Meerut Police have arrested four accused; a manhunt continues for others. An FIR is registered, and investigations are underway.

The incident has triggered strong condemnation online, with citizens demanding stricter action and respect for armed forces personnel at toll plazas.

articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A tragic incident occurred in Rishikesh on Friday evening when a couple was swept away in the Chandrabhaga river, a tributary of the Ganga. Pintu (26) and his wife Laxmi (25), residents of Chandreshwar Nagar, were crossing the river from Mayakund when strong currents pulled them away.

body.html:
A tragic incident occurred in Rishikesh on Friday evening when a couple was swept away in the Chandrabhaga river, a tributary of the Ganga.

Pintu (26) and his wife Laxmi (25), residents of Chandreshwar Nagar, were crossing the river from Mayakund when strong currents pulled them away.

Despite efforts by water police and SDRF, the couple remains untraced. The search, which began Friday night, resumed Saturday morning but yielded no results so far.

The couple, originally from Hathras, UP, sold puja items at Ganga Ghat. The incident has sparked deep concern among locals.
